replies.text: @GeographyEffect As an undergrad/masters degreed petroleum reservoir engineer who has practiced for over a decade from Shreveport, the natural gas they will use for power will definitely not come from NELA. It will undoubtedly come from the Haynesville Shale in Shreveport area pipelined over across the Northern part of the state. Haynesville wells make around 25-30 Bcf (billion cubic feet) of nat gas in their life, about half of that comes in year 1 and steadily decreases. NELA hasn't had a nat gas well or oil well drilled in over a decade. It's all shale wells now as that's most prolific. There was a nat gas reservoir in NELA drilled 50+ years ago, but that is depleted and doesn't produce nearly the same amount as the Haynesville. You might get 1 Bcf out of a NELA well in the Hosston, Cotton Valley, or Smackover formations, but nothing like the Haynesville Shale.
